issues.where: REPORT row ex:following_situations_semi_locally_simply, hypothesis 'item 3', its third question, and checklist l.65 ('⚠ strengthened: LOCALLY FINITE')
issues.problem: Local finiteness is presented as an open restriction and put to the author as a question. It is in fact a consequence of the paper's standing hypothesis at l.815: 'all topological spaces are Hausdorff, locally path-connected and first countable'. A simplicial complex with its weak topology is first countable iff it is locally finite. So no complex the paper's §3 admits is lost. The restriction is real only inside the Lean model: a non-locally-finite geometric complex of a normed space can be first countable in the subspace topology, but that is not the paper's topology.
issues.fix: Cite l.815 in the hypothesis note and in SCOPE (c): local finiteness follows from the standing first countability under the weak topology. Then either drop the third question or keep it only for non-first-countable complexes.

issues.where: GX.exists_wild_cantor_not_isSLSCIn (l.1205–1213) docstring; REPORT finding 2 of ex:wild_cantor_general_antoine
issues.problem: The corrected claim is existential: ∃ C, IsWildCantor C ∧ ¬ IsSLSCIn Cᶜ. Nothing in Lean identifies the witness as Antoine's or Blankinship's necklace; only the sorried proof of antoine_necklace_essential does. The docstring's 'there is a wild Cantor set of S³ — Antoine's necklace —' therefore names the intended witness, not something the statement certifies. The paper's sentence, read for the cited class, is universal over necklaces built by Blankinship's construction. The disclosure is honest (REPORT shows the ∃ form), so this is wording only.
issues.fix: Reword to 'there is a wild Cantor set (in the proof, Antoine's necklace) whose complement …'. Add one SCOPE sentence: the universal form over every Antoine/Blankinship necklace needs a definition of the construction, which is not made.

issues.problem: The refutation is stated for every family γ_n with the prescribed winding numbers (hγ, hγ0), but no such family is exhibited (kb/0011, last bullet). Mathematically the family exists: a free basis of π₁(ℂ∖S) supplies one. Without a witness, though, the Lean statement would remain true even if the hypotheses were unsatisfiable. This is secondary, since the theorem itself rests on a tagged sorry.

questions_for_author: l.1578: is the 'wild Cantor [general_antoine]' meant to be Antoine's or Blankinship's necklace (the cited class)? For arbitrary wild Cantor sets the claim is false. Kirkor and Skora built wild Cantor sets with simply connected complement, and for those S³ ∖ C is semi-locally simply connected in S³ (GX.isSLSCIn_compl_of_simplyConnected).

l.1572: is Γ₂ meant to be the normal closure of the [γ_n]²? The printed double cosets give all of Γ (GX.printedGamma2_eq_top). Under the normal-closure reading the fibre over (0,0) is not compact, because the dihedral quotient makes Γ/(Γ₂H₂) infinite. Was the kernel of the mod-2 winding numbers intended? For that subgroup the fibre is lim (Z/2)^{k-1}, a Cantor set, which would answer Problem 10.7.
